_doc: Revert-verify for ems__Bug 1e2f9630 (ExoSync phantom no-base conflict: base recovered from the remote history of the path), subject = historyBase.ts. Axes H* in packages/core/tests/unit/services/sync/SyncEngine.history-base.test.ts (the wiring in SyncEngine.ts is pinned by SyncEngine.history-base.spec.json). Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this spec> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/sync/historyBase.ts

M2_blob_existence_taken_as_evidence._note: Accepts a recovery whenever the path has ANY history once the local blob exists on the remote: the orphaned-blob case (a rejected push uploaded the local edit) would then overwrite a real local edit. H4 and the two orphan-blob conflicts of H11 build that input.

M3_no_existence_precheck._note: Without the git/blobs pre-check a real local edit walks the whole path history on every sync (cost, not correctness): H3 asserts no commit-list / contents request for a local edit. H10b reddens too: its failure is injected on that very pre-check, which no longer runs.
M3_no_existence_precheck.from: await getBlobText(q.transport, q.owner, q.repo, localSha, q.baseURL);

M5_list_failure_propagates._note: A failing commit-list request must leave the conflict to the merge layer, never fail the sync (H6: 502; H10a: 429).

M7_walk_capped_at_two_versions._note: H7 and H9 are the axes whose matching version sits at index 2 of the path history. H11 reddens too: its two orphan-blob conflicts then end their walk with not-found after 2 versions, BEFORE their fair share runs out, so H11's 'not fully checked' warning is no longer issued.

M15_deleting_commit_ends_walk._note: A 404 at a commit that deleted the path must skip that commit, not end the walk (reviewer LOW, probe PE).
M15_deleting_commit_ends_walk.from: continue; // 404: the commit that deleted the path — no version there

M16_rate_limit_read_as_not_found._note: Rate limit no longer told apart: a 429 still aborts (it is not a 404) but is reported as a request failure, so the three rate-limit axes see the wrong reason.

M17_failure_read_as_missing_version._note: Review round 2 MEDIUM: a timeout / 5xx read like a 404 lets the walk go on — one timeout per remaining version, silently (H13), and a failed commit list stays unreported (H6).

M18_404_not_recognized._note: A definite 404 read as a failure aborts the walk at the commit that deleted the path (H9). H3's 404 on the pre-check still ends in quarantine, as it should.
